title: Model Intake Concierge: SLA-triggered Triage and Escalation Paths
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Many enterprise customers request model additions, pins, or deprecations via support and CSM channels. Right now requests funnel into a broad intake queue that requires significant manual triage by PMs and Solutions Engineers. This increases turnaround time for SLA-bound accounts and causes missed deadlines for customers with contractual requirements (data residency, model-stability guarantees).

Problem statement:
We need an operationalized, repeatable triage flow that: 1) routes incoming model-catalog requests into defined lanes (fast-path SLA, compatibility review, compliance lane, low-priority backlog); 2) surfaces compute/compatibility blockers up-front; and 3) provides deterministic escalation windows for enterprise SLAs. Current ad-hoc routing leads to inconsistent outcomes, late notice about pinning/deprecation implications, and unclear ownership.

Goals:
- Reduce initial triage time for SLA-tier customer requests to <24 hours.
- Provide deterministic routing to one of four lanes: SLA-Fastpath, Compatibility Review, Compliance/Private, Standard Backlog.
- Auto-surface major blockers (quantization availability, region/instance constraints, model family incompatibility) in the intake form.
- Enable a concierge handshake for SLA accounts: acknowledge, estimate, and schedule canary shadow evaluation within 5 business days.

Scope (this ticket):
- Design and ship a PM-run "Model Intake Concierge" rubric + scoring rules.
- Implement intake form changes and routing flags (work with Design + Eng to change intake UI).
- Define escalation matrices and notification templates for CSM/Account owners.
- Wire basic automation that tags requests with the triage lane and priority.

Out of scope:
- Full automation of canary execution (separate infra/ENG ticket).
- Deep eval infrastructure changes (will be follow-ups).

Proposed solution:
1) Intake form: add required fields for: customer_tier, SLO_deadline, privacy_constraints, preferred_model_family, quantized_variant_needed, target_region, existing_pin_key (if any).
2) Scoring microservice: a small rules engine (hosted in PM infra namespace) returns a triage_lane and risk_score using a weighted vector: SLA_weight, compliance_flag, compute_compatibility_flag, customer_priority_score.
3) Concierge lane behavior: for SLA-Fastpath requests automatically create a short "concierge plan" doc (template in Drive) and assign a Solutions Engineer and Eng on-call; send an acknowledgement to customer with estimated cadence.
4) Compatibility lane: auto-attach a checklist for ENG to verify kernel/quantization support and recommended model variants.
5) Notifications & Escalation: templates for 24h ack, 72h update, and SLA-violation escalation into the enterprise success queue.

Acceptance criteria:
- Intake form changes are merged and live in the internal intake page.
- Triage scoring returns a lane tag for 95% of sample inputs (test set of 120 real requests).
- SLA-Fastpath handshake email template is available and used in two pilot customer cases.
- Dashboard card in Console shows "Pending Concierge" requests with age and assigned owner.

Success metrics:
- Median time to first acknowledge for SLA-tier requests <= 12 hours (target).
- % of SLA requests with a concierge plan created >= 90% within pilot accounts.
- Reduction in manual triage time per request from ~3h to <30m.

Deliverables:
- Intake form spec (Confluence doc link below).
- Scoring rules sheet + test vectors.
- Notification templates.
- Pilot runbook for 2 enterprise accounts.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: Over-automation misroutes edge-case compliance requests. Mitigation: include manual override flag and weekly review of routed items.
- Risk: Engineering capacity to implement scoring microservice. Mitigation: start with a lightweight rule-based lambda and iterate.

Next steps:
- PM to finalize the rubric (this ticket).
- Design to produce intake UI mocks by 2026-03-05.
- ENG to provide implementation estimate for the routing hook by 2026-03-10.
- Run a two-account pilot in Cycle 2026-W12.
